speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing acute diarrhea; to help you, I need to ask a few questions about your symptoms. How long have you had these symptoms, and have you noticed any blood or mucus in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Clostridioides difficile infection (C. diff). Given your recent treatment with levofloxacin for pneumonia and the onset of watery diarrhea with cramping, this is highly suggestive of antibiotic-associated colitis. We need to confirm this immediately; will you allow me to request a stool test for C. diff toxins?
